maria: Quick question — java SDK started returning 401. I discovered my API_KEY in ~/.zshrc actually has literal braces (copied from secrets manager as {abcd...}). Anyone seen braces/end markers get included and break Basic auth encoding?

sam: Yep. If your code does Basic with base64(apiKey + ':') those braces become part of the encoded string and you get a different header. Quick local check: `python -c 'import os,base64;print(base64.b64encode((os.getenv("API_KEY")+":").encode()).decode())'`

maria: Nice, thanks. How can I inspect the header from a JVM without printing the raw key? Hate dumping secrets to logs.

leo: You can reproduce without exposing the key: on your shell do `echo -n "$API_KEY:" | base64` to see what the header value should be. Or curl the endpoint with the computed header: `curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Basic $(echo -n \"$API_KEY:\" | base64)" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models` — compare 401 vs 200.

akshay: Also check for hidden chars (CR/LF) or braces with `printf %s "$API_KEY" | od -An -t x1` — 7b/7d are `{`/`}`; 0d/0a are CR/LF.

maria: Ran `od` and I see 7b at start and 7d at end. Ugh. Quick fix?

sam: Strip them: `export API_KEY=$(printf %s \"$API_KEY\" | tr -d '{}\\r\\n')` then `source ~/.zshrc` or restart the shell. If you want a zsh builtin: `typeset -Rx API_KEY=${API_KEY//[{}\n\r]/}`

leo: FYI some SDK wrappers do slightly different canonicalization. For Basic auth the canonical header is base64(API_KEY + ':') — note the colon must be appended (username with empty password). If an SDK instead expects `Authorization: Bearer` you'll want to switch accordingly. Also be careful if the API key itself contains a colon — that can confuse naive split logic.

maria: We mostly use JS/py SDKs that accept Bearer too, so I'll switch to Bearer for this service while patching onboarding docs.

akshay: Confirmed Redwood hosted API accepts `Authorization: Bearer <key>` as well. But some internal tooling still uses Basic for backwards compat. Added a short checklist for env sanity: `od` check, `echo -n | base64` check, and strip braces/cr/lf. :memo:

devex-bot: Note added to devex/auth-FAQ: "How to detect and strip surrounding braces/CRLF from API keys" with examples for bash/zsh/python/java — https://redwood.internal/docs/devex/auth-FAQ

maria: Thanks y'all — fixed locally, pushed a tiny README change for new hire onboarding that runs the `od`/base64 checks as part of the setup. PR will be up in a minute, pinging for review :pray:
